title: IT Foundations (Demo)
description: A short unofficial sample covering networking, security, and Linux basics. Use it to learn the app; replace it with a real cert pack via /create-exam.

questions.objective: Identify OSI layers and their functions
questions.stem: A router forwards packets based on IP addresses. Which OSI layer does this forwarding decision belong to?
questions.explanation: IP routing is a Network-layer (layer 3) function. Data Link addresses frames on a local segment; Transport handles TCP/UDP; Session is not used for forwarding.

questions.stem: Which of the following are RFC 1918 private IPv4 ranges? Select two.

references.title: RFC 1918 — Address Allocation for Private Internets

questions.stem: What is the default TCP port number for unencrypted HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTP listens on TCP 80 by default. Encrypted HTTP (HTTPS) uses 443.

references.title: IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry

questions.stem: TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that provides retransmission of lost segments.
questions.explanation: TCP establishes a connection (three-way handshake) and retransmits lost data. UDP is connectionless and does not retransmit.

questions.stem: An attacker reads a database of customer records but does not change them. Which CIA triad property was primarily violated?
questions.explanation: Unauthorized disclosure is a confidentiality failure. Integrity would require alteration; availability would require disruption. Non-repudiation is not part of the CIA triad.

references.title: NIST SP 800-12r1 — An Introduction to Information Security

questions.stem: Which of the following are something-you-have authentication factors? Select two.
questions.explanation: Tokens and smart cards are possession factors. A password is knowledge; a fingerprint is inherence (something you are).

questions.stem: What is the default TCP port for SSH?
questions.explanation: SSH uses TCP 22 by default. Changing the port is a common hardening step but does not replace key-based auth and firewalling.

references.title: IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry

questions.stem: HTTPS is HTTP tunneled over TLS, which provides confidentiality and integrity for the HTTP messages.
questions.explanation: HTTPS wraps HTTP in TLS. TLS encrypts the bytes (confidentiality) and authenticates the stream (integrity). It does not by itself authenticate the user.

questions.stem: Which command is the modern preferred way to list TCP listening sockets on Linux?
questions.explanation: `ss` replaces netstat for socket stats. `-lnt` lists listening TCP sockets numerically. ifconfig is interface config; chmod changes mode; dig queries DNS.

questions.stem: A file mode of 644 means which of the following? Select two.
questions.explanation: 6 is rw- for owner, 4 is r-- for group and others. Nobody has execute; group does not have write.

questions.stem: Which command changes the permission bits of a file on Linux? Enter the command name only.
questions.explanation: `chmod` changes mode bits. `chown` changes ownership; `umask` sets the default mask for new files.

questions.stem: On a typical Linux system, the root account has user ID 0.
questions.explanation: UID 0 is the superuser. The login name is usually `root`, but the kernel grants privilege by UID.
